text: {"question":"How does empirically calibrating the primordial helium fraction with the Large Binocular Telescope measurement restore the ability of the cosmic microwave background to constrain the baryon density (ωb) and the effective number of relativistic species (Neff) to the same precision as when the standard BBN relation is imposed?","reference_answer":"By fixing YHe to the observed LBT value, the analysis removes the dependence on theoretical BBN predictions, thereby preserving the sensitivity of the CMB to the free‑electron fraction. This empirical calibration recovers the same precision on ωb and Neff that would be achieved if the standard BBN relation were enforced, as shown in Figure 1 of the conclusions.","passage_1_contribution":"The abstract states that the LBT measurement enables cosmological constraints that are agnostic to BBN but as precise as those enforcing standard BBN predictions.","passage_2_contribution":"The conclusions explain that empirically calibrating YHe with the LBT measurement recovers the constraining power on ωb and Neff lost when relaxing the BBN assumption, illustrated in Figure 1.","joint_reason":"The question asks for the mechanism by which the LBT measurement restores parameter constraints, requiring the specific evidence that the empirical calibration recovers the precision on ωb and Neff, which is only provided in the conclusions.","same_quantity":true}
